checks: The revision specifies δ and both branches of f. Positivity and convexity are valid on the full real domain, so the input argument need not stay above the join.
The middle support inequalities in the proof divide by H(n)>0 to give the exact cut g_(K−y)(x−y)+εf(1+a·(x−y))≤1. Thus the named target in the statement has a definite interpretation.

The positive cutoff region has Δ<2η, so its field coefficient s is positive. When Δ≤η the average input cut yields the target after spending Δ against εf≤1. When Δ>η, the old midpoint has uniform slack at least η and the bounded target field fits that slack. This check does not require y∈M.

checks: Since H has positive minimum, the active cutoff band has s>min H/2. The other cutoff coefficient is nonnegative with positive old support distance. This makes the fields continuous, nonnegative and convex in the physical point.
The two normal-dependent centers average to y even when y is outside M. At Δ≤η, Jensen gives the midpoint cut with coefficient s; the lost Δ gap permits raising it to H uniformly for small ε.
For Δ>η, nestedness places the midpoint in the old M, with more than η old slack. The bounded target field fits this slack uniformly, including the transition band.
